title: Addressing
summary: How channels get addresses and how tags make programs independent of them, across different PLC platforms.

sections.heading: Address styles
sections.body: The same channel has different names on different platforms: `%IX0.0` (IEC), `%I0.0` (Siemens), `Local:1:I.Data.0` (Rockwell), a linked variable (Beckhoff) or `X0` (Mitsubishi). The **I/O map** connects addresses to tags.

sections.heading: From channel to tag
sections.body: The program only sees the tag.
sections.diagram: slot 1, channel 0 --> address (platform style) --> tag StartPB --> program

sections.heading: Platform profiles
sections.body: Switch the platform profile of a free lab to see the addresses change while the program stays the same.

sections.heading: Common mistake
sections.body: Moving a module or changing its start address while the program uses absolute addresses: every address shifts. Tags survive such changes.

question.question: Which address style is typical for Rockwell Logix controllers?

sections.heading: Compare platforms
sections.body: Create a free lab with the Siemens S7-1200 profile and one with the generic profile, then compare the addresses in the Hardware tab.

sections.heading: Summary and troubleshooting note
sections.body:
Addresses identify channels in a platform-specific style; tags give them meaning and keep programs portable.

**Troubleshooting note:** When a signal appears on the wrong tag, check the I/O map and the module's start address before touching the wiring.
